name: Dirty Three
label: Touch and Go
lede: A violinist, a guitarist and a drummer worked up a set in Warren Ellis's kitchen and played it that night in a Melbourne pub with no stage. Thirty-odd years and nine albums later, there's still no singer.

eras.title: A pub with no stage
eras.text: Turner and White had played together for years, including in the art-punk band Venom P. Stinger; Ellis was a classically trained violinist who'd taught school in country Victoria and busked around Europe. Together they found a sound loud enough to need no singer, and by 1994 they were opening for Pavement and the Beastie Boys.

years.cap: Flyer for the Baker's Arms, Saturdays April 18 and 25, 1992
q: You had to take risks with Dirty Three, always.
years.h: Rehearsal in Ellis's kitchen, first gig the same night
years.p: On Anzac Day the trio put a set together and play it at the Baker's Arms Hotel. No stage, no PA, no bass drum; Ellis holds a pickup on his violin with a rubber band.
years.xp:
They kept playing the Baker's Arms regularly, NPR reports, and turned down friends' advice to find a singer. Ellis: what they were doing felt expressive enough. Turner's addition to the band's founding principles: free drinks.

The rubber-banded pickup is why the violin came out distorted and drenched in feedback, nothing like a violin is supposed to sound.

years.h: Twelve songs taped in Turner's bedroom
years.p: The self-titled cassette is recorded at what they called Scuzz Studio, Turner's bedroom. In 1993 the band gives copies away at gigs.

q: Walking onstage after the Dirty Three is like walking on hot coals.
years.h: Pavement get blown off their own stage in Melbourne
years.p: Dirty Three open for [[Pavement|36bfa85f-737b-41db-a8fc-b8825850ffc3]] in Melbourne, then across US clubs. Bob Nastanovich says following them, dozens of times, never got easier.
years.xp: The connection came through Stephen Pavlovic, whose Fellaheen label released American indie bands in Australia. That year Dirty Three also supported the [[Beastie Boys|9beb62b2-88db-4cea-801e-162cd344ee53]] and the [[Jon Spencer Blues Explosion|d1ab8ca8-fb9f-4e78-a422-3cd5406dc0b1]].

years.cap: Poster for Pavement's Australian tour, July 1994
years.h: Torn & Frayed puts out a self-titled CD
years.p: The band's first CD, on the Australian label Torn & Frayed. Ian McFarlane heard subtle and dramatic violin, tensile guitar and sympathetic drumming.

yt: I Remember a Time When Once You Used to Love Me, Meredith, 1994
years.h: Sad & Dangerous, partly salvaged from the bedroom tape
years.p: Released on Poon Village and built partly from the 1992 cassette. Tours with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]], [[John Cale|72c090b6-a68e-4cb9-b330-85278681a714]] and Pavement follow, and lead to Touch and Go.

years.src: Wikipedia: Warren Ellis · Wikipedia: Dirty Three
years.h: Nick Cave borrows the violinist
years.p: Invited in 1993 to play on a few songs for Let Love In, Ellis ends up a full member of [[Nick Cave and the Bad Seeds|172e1f1a-504d-4488-b053-6344ba63e6d0]].
years.xp: It grew into a second career: the Bad Seeds, Grinderman, and a run of film scores with Cave from The Proposition to Blonde. Cave, for his part, has called Dirty Three his favourite live band, no contest, because there's no singer.

eras.title: America, with the drums on the roof
eras.text: Touch and Go signed them and America got them four times in 1995 alone. They built an audience the way agent David Viecelli remembers it: people saw them once and told their friends, partly for the music and partly for Ellis's long, strange stories between songs.

years.cap: Poster for the Great American Music Hall, San Francisco, March 10, 1995
yt: Live at the Middle East, Cambridge, March 29, 1995
years.h: The first US tour opens in San Francisco
years.p: In May they play Music West in Vancouver; by year's end they've toured the US four times, then Greece, Germany and the UK.

years.h: Touch and Go issues Dirty Three in America
years.p: Recorded in Melbourne's Studio 325 in 1993–94 with Phil McKellar, with a longer Kim's Dirt than on Sad & Dangerous. NPR says the US push even included Lollapalooza's second stage.

years.h: Turner buys a gold car and straps White's drums to the roof
years.p: Booking agent David Viecelli remembers it as a Duster or a Galaxie 500. The drums rode outside the whole tour, through heat and rain, until they were wrecked.
years.xp:
Viecelli has booked them in the US since the first visits. His memory of seeing them: some of it bewildering and disorienting, some of it incredibly charming, and nothing else like it.

White's habits stayed the same for decades. Will Oldham told NPR the drummer toured with a suitcase of books and rocks, wore the same suit daily, and went hiking in dress shoes and a pink shirt.

years.h: A live score for The Passion of Joan of Arc, with Nick Cave
years.p: After touring Israel with the Bad Seeds, the trio and Cave accompany Carl Dreyer's silent film at the National Film Theatre in London.

years.cap: Big Day Out running order, Sydney Showground, January 1996
years.h: Cave walks on at the Melbourne Big Day Out
years.p: Dirty Three play the Big Day Out tour, and at the Melbourne stop Cave joins them onstage.

years.src: Touch and Go Records: Horse Stories · Wikipedia: Horse Stories · Wikipedia: Dirty Three
years.h: Horse Stories, recorded in London, lands in Rolling Stone's top three
years.p: Made at Maison Rouge Studios and released by Touch and Go. I Remember a Time When Once You Used to Love Me is a cover of a song by the Greek singer Arleta.
years.xp: Entertainment Weekly gave it an A and Alternative Press a 5 out of 5; it was nominated for two ARIA Awards the next year. Like almost every Dirty Three album after it, the cover is a Turner painting.
play: I Remember a Time When Once You Used to Love Me

years.src: Wikipedia: Ocean Songs · Touch and Go Records: Ocean Songs · Wikipedia: Dirty Three
years.h: Steve Albini records the quiet one
years.p: Cut at [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]]'s Electrical Audio in Chicago in August and September 1997, with [[David Grubbs|f72e65e9-3ee7-4dce-9c53-5dc6221f6cd3]] on piano and harmonium. Touch and Go's TG193 reaches No. 44 in Australia.
years.xp:
AllMusic called it the band's most controversial record and a decided change of direction: every tempo held back, like waves. Rolling Stone Australia noted Ellis playing without distortion for the first time. Billboard's Chris Morris heard the same band, still brazenly live, gone rapturous instead of explosive.

In 2010 it was named in the book 100 Best Australian Albums.

years.src: Wikipedia: Warren Ellis · Wikipedia: Dirty Three
years.h: Ellis moves to Paris
years.p: From here the band lives on three continents: Ellis in Paris, White eventually in New York, Turner in Melbourne. They also score John Curran's film Praise.

eras.title: Singers allowed, briefly
eras.text: The records got longer and sadder, then shorter and stranger. The band picked up a superfan in Chan Marshall (Cat Power), toured Asia, and curated its own festival, while Turner and White became the rhythm section half of indie rock wanted.

years.h: Whatever You Love, You Are wins the ARIA
years.p: Best Adult Alternative Album at the 2000 ARIA Awards. Ian McFarlane heard the band moving toward John Coltrane.

years.h: Dirty Three and Low share a fish tank
years.p: Recorded in 1999 for Konkurrent's In the Fishtank series, the session with [[Low|42faad37-8aaa-42e4-a300-5a7dae79ed24]] comes out as In the Fishtank 7.

years.h: On tour in Taiwan with Cat Power
years.p: The trio tours Taiwan with Chan Marshall and goes back with her in 2004. Turner and White had already backed her on record.

years.h: She Has No Strings Apollo
years.p: NPR's Hank Shteamer hears this one and Whatever You Love, You Are sprawling out with elegiac splendor.

years.h: A storm rolls in on their Meredith set and they play through it
years.p: At the Meredith Music Festival in Victoria the rain threatened to wreck the show. The set came out the next year as Live! At Meredith.
years.xp: Ellis, remembering it later: "we just went out and played like our lives depended on it."

years.h: Cinder: nineteen tracks, two voices
years.p: Shorter pieces, each member recorded separately, and guest vocals on two tracks from Chan Marshall and [[The Mekons|66d2169c-dea5-46d3-b4cb-52ed87b24ab0]]' Sally Timms.
years.xp: Marshall, in the band's documentary, described an addiction to Dirty Three and said she was completely shocked they'd want a vocalist. NPR later corrected a claim that these were the band's first vocals: there had been earlier ones.

years.cap: Dirty Three in Faenza, Italy, May 2007
years.h: Dirty Three book their own All Tomorrow's Parties
years.p: The band curates a weekend of the festival with bands it admires and plays twice itself. In November a two-DVD set adds a Tokyo concert and Darcy Maine's documentary.

eras.title: The ocean again, then the low sun
eras.text: With the members busy elsewhere, Dirty Three became an occasional band: a classic album played whole, then one record after a seven-year gap, made back home in Melbourne.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ocean Songs · Wikipedia: Dirty Three
years.h: Ocean Songs played start to finish at ATP New York
years.p: The 1998 album gets a full live performance at All Tomorrow's Parties in New York; they'd already done it in London in 2005.
years.xp: A September 2009 performance of the album became the bonus live recording on the 2021 deluxe Ocean Songs reissue.

years.src: Wikipedia: Toward the Low Sun · Wikipedia: Dirty Three
years.h: Seven years after Cinder, Toward the Low Sun
years.p: Recorded in Melbourne at Head Gap and Sing Sing, out on Drag City and Bella Union. It reaches No. 31 in Australia; in March they play the Sydney Opera House.

years.h: Turner paints the covers
years.p: An exhibited painter, Mick Turner has done the art for nearly every Dirty Three album and runs the band's own label, Anchor & Hope.

years.cap: Hardly Strictly Bluegrass, San Francisco, October 2012
years.h: A bluegrass festival in Golden Gate Park takes the trio
years.p: On the Toward the Low Sun tour, Dirty Three play San Francisco's Hardly Strictly Bluegrass. In November the tour reaches Manchester Cathedral.

eras.title: Everest with a wheelbarrow
eras.text: After shows at the Sydney Opera House in 2019, the three got back in a room in Melbourne and came out with a six-part suite. The 2024 tour was their first major one since 2012.

years.cap: Ellis at the Sydney Opera House, May 2019
years.h: Back together at the Sydney Opera House
years.p: The Opera House stages Dirty Three and an on-stage conversation with the band, their last live shows until 2024.

years.src: NPR · Wikipedia: Love Changes Everything · Wikipedia: Dirty Three
yt: Love Changes Everything I, official video
years.h: Love Changes Everything: one title, six parts
years.p: Six variations on one theme, 41 minutes, out on Drag City and Bella Union. It reaches No. 12 in Australia, their highest chart placing.
years.xp:
Ellis told NPR it couldn't have been made 30 years earlier: it came from trusting each other enough to get in a room and see what happened. Describing the early days, he compared the band to explorers climbing Everest. "With a wheelbarrow," White added, and all three cracked up.

Asked if they keep up with each other's projects, Turner said: "We don't stalk each other." It made the 2024 Australian Music Prize shortlist.

years.cap: Ellis and White at the Enmore Theatre, Sydney, June 2024
years.h: The first big Australian tour since 2012
years.p: The Love Changes Everything tour earns an ARIA nomination for Best Australian Live Act.

years.h: Europe in the winter, North America in the spring
years.p: A European tour runs through November and December 2025, with North American dates set for March and April 2026.
